Subject: MPA action-grid: orderform velocity & pilot-signature path

Hi Sanjay / Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum for the pilot, I pulled together a short Mutual Action Plan (attached) that separates the minimal path to start work (order form + SOW) from the parallel MSA/DPA redline process. High level asks:

- Can procurement confirm that an order form signed by procurement is sufficient to issue a PO for the pilot? If not, what exact legal gating do you need before PO issuance?
- Can HelioMed accept the proposed single-signature path for the pilot (Order Form + limited SOW) while the MSA/DPA go through legal review in parallel?
- Please flag any internal approvals (VP/Finance) that will add time so we can sequence the MAP.

Attached: MPA_action_grid_v1.xlsx (action grid with owners & dates), OrderForm_HelioMed_draft.pdf (clean order form for signature), SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf (high-level evidence to help security team).

Our proposed compressed timeline if we get a green light on the single-sign path:
- Week 0 (today): Sign order form + SOW -> PO issued by HelioMed finance
- Week 1: Onboarding kickoff; limited pilot data flow; Redwood provides SOC2/attestations
- Weeks 1–3: Legal redlines on MSA/DPA; if material, we’ll add an addendum for the pilot scope to avoid blocking initial work

If useful, I can update the MPA to include explicit VP approval steps — flagging Rachel on finance timing. Can you share the internal PO cadence (how many business days to approve after signature)?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez

Subject: Re: MPA action-grid: orderform velocity & pilot-signature path

Alex —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few quick notes from procurement/ops perspective:

1) Order form alone typically can be used to raise a PO for pilots up to $50k, provided the finance approver signs off. We will need to confirm the exact cost bucket once Redwood finalizes estimated usage in the SOW.
2) Legal (looping Emily) will want to see the MSA redlines; if there are any security/data residency clauses that are not standard we will need sign-off before production data flows. For a limited pilot, we can accept a signed Order Form with a narrow SOW as long as the SOW explicitly limits data types and retention.
3) Our VP of Engineering sometimes requires a 5–7 business day review for integrations — that can be the main timing impact.

Next steps from our side: I’ll confirm the PO timeline with finance (Rachel?) and get back with the expected business days. Emily — can you confirm if legal is OK with a parallel MSA review while we execute an order form for the pilot?

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Procurement, HelioMed
sanjay.rao@heliomed.com

Hi Sanjay / Emily —

Thanks for the quick response. From Redwood Legal’s perspective we are comfortable with the parallel path you proposed provided we put a short-term protective addendum in place that covers pilot scope and data handling while the MSA/DPA go through redlines. Suggested approach:

- Order Form + SOW: limited-scope SOW (duration, ROI metrics, data classes) — single authorized signatory from HelioMed is acceptable to trigger PO and onboarding.
- Pilot Addendum (one page): confirms limited data use, retention window, and rollback plan. This addendum would be attached to the Order Form for the pilot and sunset when MSA/DPA are finalized.
- MSA/DPA: Redwood will accept tracked changes; can we get legal redlines within 10 business days? If critical clauses are called out, we can agree interim mitigations to keep pilot live.

I attached a short redline checklist to the MPA (owner = Redwood Legal) and highlighted two items we can proactively remove from the pilot-scope SOW to reduce friction: (1) analytics export retention >90 days, (2) cross-app access to raw user content.

If Helen or the legal team prefers a short working session, happy to block 30 minutes this week to go through the checklist.

Chloe Martin
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
